about: Trigger eval queries for this skill's description. A query is labelled with whether the skill should activate for it; the negatives are near-misses that share vocabulary with the skill but need something else. Split fixed so successive description edits are compared on the same ground: tune against train, judge against validation. `stop refining my questions` (validation) was reviewed under the same criterion (issues #25, #24) and its positive label stands, though the case fires 0x. The criterion asks what complying requires, and here it requires a write: Phase 4 lists `stop refining` by name as a mid-session rule change that updates the config file with `Edit`, and the SessionStart hook reloads `refine_question` every session, so a stop that is not persisted does not stop anything past this one. `lingua off` is not the sharper phrasing to swap in -- it carries the magic word, so it fires whatever the description says, and the body has it suspend for the session without writing the file, making it the less persistent of the two. Relabelling would assert something the body contradicts, and replacing the query would delete the evidence, which is the asymmetry against `restate my question before you answer it` at 3/3: same skill, same vocabulary, opposite results. So this is recorded as a body-versus-description mismatch -- the description names the on-state and never the off-state -- and the failing case is left standing as the observation that would justify fixing it.
how_to_run: `make eval` is the committed runner, but it covers only the queries a 3-sample blind-router baseline actually missed, not this whole file -- see CLAUDE.md for why 13 and not 380. To judge the rest: `skillgrade` runs a labelled set like this one and exits non-zero when the pass rate falls below a threshold. Needing nothing installed: run each query with `claude -p --output-format json` and count the runs whose transcript contains a Skill tool_use naming this skill. Cheapest of all, and closest to the router's real conditions: give a model only the name and description of every installed skill, with no bodies and no repo access, and have it pick one skill or none per query. `claude plugin eval`, which `make eval` drives, is generally available rather than early access; what it needs instead is a credential, a network and real money -- $0.142 a run, measured -- which is why it sits outside `make test` and CI does not run it. It will not reproduce this file query-for-query either: a bare query does not fire a skill, so a case is one of these queries rewritten as a realistic turn. This file stays the cheap, free, offline record.
